articleTitle: Interconnections of National Grid Company UK with Scotland and France
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on System Interconnection and Energy Exchange Across National Boundaries
abstract: The author examines the implications of interconnecting electrical power systems in the light of experience gained by National Grid Company UK (NGC) and its predecessors over the past 40 years on the interconnections with Scotland and France. The author addresses the planning, operational, commercial interfaces as well as customs and practices which influenced the developing use of the inter-connections. Future trends likely to effect the interconnections are also analysed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on System Interconnection and Energy Exchange Across National Boundaries
abstract: The major part of the world's primary energy resources lies in the developing world. Trans-national power transfers between developing countries depend mainly on the availability of generation surpluses for the longer term. The author looks at the energy quantities exchanged, supply conditions, tied schemes and utility cooperation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Planning international interconnections at EDF: technical and economic aspects
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on System Interconnection and Energy Exchange Across National Boundaries
abstract: Planning a power system consists of taking decisions about investments in order to meet future demand with an acceptable quality of service while minimizing the overall costs. The authors present EDF's approach in the field of interconnection planning: the study organization, the evaluation of economic savings and technical advantages brought by the planned network, and some concrete examples of such recent studies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Latest proposals for legislation relating to EC internal energy markets
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on System Interconnection and Energy Exchange Across National Boundaries
abstract: As part of the move towards achieving a single European Market by the end of 1992, the Commission of the European Community, and in particular its Directorates General for Energy and Competition, have been increasingly insistent that the principles of the single market are applied to energy, a sector characterised to date by monopolistic practices and a market partitioned along national lines. The author looks at existing, legislation; new initiatives of the Commission; Eurelectrics position and proposals; the position of the UK supply industry; and future action.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Control of power flow between systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on System Interconnection and Energy Exchange Across National Boundaries
abstract: When MW capacity and MWh energy interchange contracts are made between neighbouring utilities, economic benefits are expected by both parties. If energy interchange is arranged as part of the normal scheduling of generators for economic dispatch, then to fulfil contracts entered into in advance, power flow levels and their duration must be scheduled across interconnecting transmission circuits. Maintaining the scheduled flows is part of the duties of the system control engineer, but the costing of the use of the system for them is an economic operational planning problem. The author outlines methods available to the control engineer to meet scheduled interchange flows on a high voltage transmission system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Operation of the Belgian Power System within UCPTE
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on System Interconnection and Energy Exchange Across National Boundaries
abstract: The Belgian Power System is interconnected with the UCPTE through six 380 kV lines directly with France and the Netherlands, the sum of the thermal capacities being over 8000 MVA. The author describes physical and contractual exchanges between Belgium and UCPTE countries including exchanges of emergency power. Power system operation in the normal state and operation during emergencies and restoration are described. Control centre organisation is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Use of system costing for energy exchange
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on System Interconnection and Energy Exchange Across National Boundaries
abstract: In setting up energy and capacity exchange contracts, the cost of using the system to effect the exchange must be estimated. This cost will depend upon at least two factors, namely: cost of losses and system operating cost (per MWh); and system infrastructure cost to pay for plant and any necessary reinforcement (per MW). The problem then is to allocate a charge for use-of-system which is seen to be fairly divided between fixed and variable costs. This is not unlike charging for a power supply to any customer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on System Interconnection and Energy Exchange Across National Boundaries
abstract: The author looks at the present status of the operations management in the interconnected nordic system by the end of 1991. The power industry including the association of Nordel is in the process of change and development within the EC and the concept of an open market for electricity regardless of boundaries.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
